title: Safe OpenCode maintenance and exact client recovery

statements.text: Preserve exact pane/session mappings, owning and viewed identities, canonical directories, duplicate views, layout and focus.
Preserve active sessions, background work, pending forms, permissions and unexported client input; uncertain state cannot authorize disruption.
Implement and validate in isolated disposable state without live OpenCode or Herdr restart, signal, input, configuration deployment or database mutation.
Keep the native installer as the sole executable owner and reuse the existing capture owner and bounded locks.

Retain immutable checkpoint generations, uncertain mappings and per-pane recovery assessments. Executable recovery and action journaling require later qualified native capabilities and separate approval.
Native atomic drain, client-state export and passive attach are unqualified; wrapper locks and polling cannot prevent all concurrent submissions.
The operator approves the two-context map and one source-only draft pull request.
Activation and replacement refuse whenever preservation cannot be proved; current native capability gaps remain hard blockers without force overrides.
Add a separate explicit maintenance command and preserve existing native managed update/restart behavior.
Keep private runtime identities and credentials outside public source; validate publication through the existing repository authority.
Use isolated regression evidence and exact launch approval before implementation registration; report unsupported capabilities without fabricated passes.
Do not modify upstream OpenCode or Herdr source, add a second updater daemon, restore old databases, or deploy this delivery to running systems.
A supported read-only V2 CLI observer records exact route and tabs; no live registration or generated Herdr integration edits occur. Draft and passive-detach capability remains unknown.
